- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (e.g., >0.80) and underperform when sentiment is bearish (e.g., <0.27).  
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- Underestimate in early forecast windows (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; adjust upward slightly.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment strongly supports.  
- Lagged sentiment effects: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days prior, forecast should adjust downward slightly to reflect delayed market reaction.  
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs: if last 3–5 days are trending up, cap forecast rise to 3–5% below true outcome to prevent runaway momentum.
